DUO suppresses cells below 5 ('<5'); 13 such cells were excluded, so the true figure lies between 6649 and 6701. 03b still counts students who were previously enrolled in hbo (or who hold an hbo degree). Alternative DUO file 03a (first-time in higher education at all, full-time wo-bachelor) gives 5154 (+14 suppressed cells). Domestic-only entrants are not available in the DUO files. Applicants: not found / not published at institution level for 2023/24 in the sources opened. Studielink application counts per institution are not in DUO open data; the Universiteiten van Nederland page 'Aanmeldingen bacheloropleidingen' returned HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch (not bypassed). Admitted: no institution-wide count (offers exist only for numerus fixus programmes). Places: empty because most bachelor's programmes have no capacity cap (admission by right with a VWO diploma, WHW 7.24); capacities exist only for numerus fixus programmes (see below). sel_unit refers to the entrant count (persons); no applicant count was entered. Regime 'mixed': open admission with a VWO diploma for most programmes, own selection by the institution (decentral selection, WHW 7.53) for numerus fixus programmes; Studielink is an application portal, not an allocator. Cross-check: DUB (UU independent news site, 11 Feb 2025) reports 'In 2023, UU counted 6,510 freshers' (definition not stated). Entrants include University College Roosevelt (Middelburg). Older DUB articles with Studielink application counts (12,315 / 12,603 applications) refer to earlier years (2016 and earlier) and were not used. Equity: no. WHW 7.53 (version 1 Sep 2023) allows selection for capped programmes only on at least two qualitative criteria and/or (unweighted or criteria-weighted) lottery; the RUG summary of the law states that from 2013 until 1 Sep 2023 only selection on at least two qualitative criteria was possible and that criteria must be the same for all candidates at every stage. No national rule reserving places, adding points, lowering thresholds or opening a separate track for disadvantaged groups was found. WHW 7.53(3) requires institutions to 'take into account the interests' of applicants from the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom (in practice: same procedure, remote testing) - a consideration, not a reservation or lower threshold; not coded. The 'Wet herinvoering loting bij numerus fixus' (in force 1 Sep 2023, motivated by kansengelijkheid) adds lottery options, not group-targeted preference. The 21+ entrance exam (colloquium doctum, WHW 7.29) is age-based, not disadvantage-defined. UU Reglement Inschrijving en Collegegeld 2023-2024 refers to a separate 'Reglement selectie voor numerus fixus bacheloropleidingen', which was not found/opened (one search); list of UU numerus fixus programmes and capacities for 2023/24 not recorded. Equity coded no on national-law evidence; UU's own selection regulation unverified.

adm_notes: Applicants: not found at institution level for 2023/24 (no institution-wide applicant or offer counts located; German admission statistics are kept per programme and per procedure - local NC procedures run by the institution, often via DoSV, and the central procedure for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary medicine run by the Stiftung fuer Hochschulzulassung). Admitted: empty for the same reason. Places: empty - most first-degree programmes have no capacity cap (zulassungsfrei), so no institution-wide intake capacity exists; caps (Zulassungszahlen) exist only for restricted programmes. Entrants = Destatis Statistischer Bericht 'Statistik der Studierenden WS 2023/2024' (published 9 Aug 2024), table 21311-06 / csv-21311-06, column Studierende_Anfaenger_1HS_Deutsche (German nationals in their first semester at any German higher education institution, WS 2023/24 only; the summer-semester 2024 intake is not included). Domestic proxy = German nationality (foreign Bildungsinlaender are counted as Auslaender). 1HS counts all degree types, not only first-degree; for German nationals almost all first-semester students are first-degree entrants (assumption, not verified). sel_unit refers to the entrant headcount (persons); no applicant count was entered. All nationalities, 1HS: 9145 (of which 5198 foreign - large international master's intake). TUM's statistical report 'TUM in Zahlen 2023' (mediatum.ub.tum.de/doc/1774468/1774468.pdf), which a search snippet suggests contains programme-level application counts (e.g. Engineering Science), returned an Anubis anti-bot challenge page to both curl and WebFetch and had no Wayback capture (the Internet Archive was offline when accessed). It was not bypassed, so TUM applicant counts are unknown rather than 'not published'. Regime 'mixed': the current TUM page says most programmes use the Eignungsfeststellungsverfahren (an aptitude assessment run by TUM: own admission without a capacity cap); other programmes are zulassungsfrei or NC (capped), plus the central procedure for medicine. Equity coded yes on the hardship quota (Haertefallquote / Vorabquote fuer Faelle aussergewoehnlicher Haerte): Staatsvertrag ueber die Hochschulzulassung 2019 Art. 9(1) No. 1 reserves places in every capped procedure for applicants for whom rejection would be an 'aussergewoehnliche Haerte'; Land law implements it for local procedures. It applies only in admission-restricted first-degree programmes (local NC and the central procedure), hence equity_scope some_programmes. Basis: hardship is assessed individually; the recognised grounds are mainly health/disability (illness with a tendency to worsen, career choice restricted by disability) and special social or family circumstances. Limited finances are explicitly NOT a recognised ground (FU Merkblatt), and a severe-disability certificate alone is not sufficient. Basis is therefore coded disability;other (other = individual social/family hardship). CHECKER: this is a judgement call. The quota is a formal reserved-places rule, but eligibility rests on individual hardship rather than membership of a disadvantaged group; the coordinator may prefer to recode it to no, for consistency with countries where individual hardship clauses were not coded. Also present but not coded as an instrument: Nachteilsausgleich (StV Art. 8(2)). On application, the grade or waiting time is replaced by the value the applicant would have reached without hindrances outside their control (illness, disability, pregnancy, family care); this is an individual score correction, not a group threshold. Excluded as not equity: quotas for non-EU foreigners, second degrees, Bundeswehr medical officers, Landarztquote and public-health-service obligations (service obligations), vocationally qualified applicants and top athletes. equity_reserved_places and filled counts: not published (no institution-level count of hardship admissions found). mandate national_law = Interstate Treaty on university admission ratified by all Laender, plus Land admission statutes; government_regulation = Land admission ordinances. Bavaria: the hardship quota is 2% of places in local procedures (BayHZG Art. 5(3) No. 1), read only in the current consolidated text valid from 01.04.2026; the 2023/24 text was not read, so the 2% for 2023/24 assumes the rule did not change. In the central procedure (medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary medicine) it is 1% under the current HZV § 6(1) No. 1 (text valid from 01.05.2026) but was 2% in the original HZV of 10 Feb 2020 (GVBl. 4/2020); the central-procedure share in force for 2023/24 entry was not determined. equity_reserved_share_pct = 2 refers to the local procedure only. At TUM the hardship quota reaches only the NC (capped) programmes and medicine. Per the LMU page (same Bavarian law), programmes with Eignungsfeststellungsverfahren are not admission-restricted, so no hardship application exists there; since most TUM bachelor programmes use aptitude assessment, coverage is narrow. equity_confidence is low because no TUM-specific 2023/24 rule or list of TUM NC programmes was opened. | [coded out] equity_scope=some_programmes | [coded out] equity_instrument=reserved_places | [coded out] equity_mandate=national_law;government_regulation | [coded out] equity_reserved_share_pct=2

Equity: yes, two institutional schemes for 2023 entry, both admitting on a published reduced ATAR below the course's guaranteed selection rank. (1) MySydney Entry and Scholarship Scheme (Wayback capture 15 Dec 2022): 'every eligible student starting in 2023' gets 'entry on a reduced ATAR'; eligibility = domestic student residing in an area in the bottom 25 percent of the ABS SEIFA Index of Education and Occupation, assessed automatically by UAC; course table gives guaranteed selection rank vs MySydney ATAR, e.g. B Arts 80 vs 70, B Commerce 96 vs 85, B Architecture and Environments 85 vs 80, B Science/D Medicine 99.95 vs 99.5 (indicative). (2) E12 Early Offer and Scholarship Scheme (capture 5 Oct 2022, 'eligible for E12 in 2023'): applicants assessed by UAC's Educational Access Scheme as experiencing financial hardship (F01A-F01D), residing in a lowest-25% SEIFA area (AG01), or having attended a NSW rural or regional school (S01R, S01C), plus principal support via the Schools Recommendation Scheme; 'formal UAC offer in the main offer round by meeting a reduced E12 ATAR' (e.g. B Arts/B Advanced Studies 80 vs 70; B Commerce/B Advanced Studies 96 vs 85); some health courses marked 'Limited E12 places available' (no number stated). Both schemes cover most of the undergraduate course list across faculties, hence all_programmes. Basis: income_or_socioeconomic (financial hardship, low-SES area); region_or_rural (E12 rural/regional school). No reserved share or number of places stated; number of 2023 entrants admitted under MySydney/E12 not found within budget. Not opened: University of Sydney Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander pathways (Gadigal program) and UAC EAS adjustment factors at Sydney for 2023 (these could add race_ethnicity / separate_track; checker may verify). Mandate institutional; no national law or regulation requiring equity admission found. Not counted: Dalyell Scholars, Academic Excellence, Future Leaders schemes (merit/leadership), scholarships (financial aid).

Equity (Undergraduate Prospectus 2023 Admission, p.15, Wayback capture 2023-01-17 of the UCT PDF): (1) 'Redress on the basis of disadvantage': a disadvantage factor of 0-10% (0-20% for Health Sciences programmes) derived from the applicant's school and family background is added to the Faculty Points Score (FPS) to give a Weighted Points Score (WPS) -> bonus_points, basis income_or_socioeconomic (school and home disadvantage); (2) 'Redress for diversity': South African applicants are categorised by their parents' apartheid-era race classification (redress categories 1-4: Black, Coloured, Indian, Chinese) and the categories are used to give priority in selection to meet diversity targets set for each programme/plan; selection is in Band A (unweighted FPS), Band B (WPS, 'usually a bigger proportion') and Band C (remaining places filled in FPS rank order from redress categories) -> reserved_places (Band C places; size not stated) and basis race_ethnicity. The 2023 Directions for Undergraduate Applicants say the redress and diversity policies apply to SA applicants whose parent(s) were classified Black, Coloured, Chinese or Indian under apartheid. (3) Academic Development programmes (Commerce example, p.28): SA Black, Chinese, Coloured or Indian applicants with a disadvantage factor > 1.0 may apply, with lower FPS thresholds (Band C rows) -> lower_cutoff. Scope all_programmes: the band system applies to each programme/plan. Mandate institutional (UCT admissions policy); no national law requiring this rule was cited (not searched). Band proportions and per-programme diversity targets are not stated in the prospectus -> reserved share/places empty (not_published in sources opened); filled counts not found. Disputable coding for a checker: whether Band C 'diversity targets' count as reserved_places (they are targets met by priority, not a fixed quota).

Unit: first-preference applicants are unique persons (each applicant has one first preference); applicants listing UB at any preference are larger (table 1.1.2, not entered). Regime: central_allocation - pre-enrolment in Catalan public universities is run by the Generalitat's Oficina d'Accés a la Universitat, which assigns places by admission score and preference order. Equity (Catalan pre-enrolment, 2023): 5% of places in all grado programmes reserved for students with a recognised disability >=33% (RD 412/2014 art. 26, national basic regulation in force until 12 June 2024); one place per 'centre d'estudi' (study offer) reserved for students in or formerly in the care of the DGAIA (child protection; reserve kept until the calendar year the student turns 21 in 2023); one place per study offer reserved for students included in the Generalitat's Programa del Poble Gitano (Roma). The care-leaver and Roma reserves are coded as basis 'other' (care-experienced) and 'race_ethnicity' (Roma). Their legal instrument is reported (search results and 2018 press coverage, not opened as primary text) to be agreements of the Comissió d'Accés i Afers Estudiantils of the Consell Interuniversitari de Catalunya; the agreement texts were not opened, so mandate is coded government_regulation (national RD for disability; regional interuniversity council agreements for the other two) with that caveat. The rule text quoted is from a secondary school's May 2023 information sheet (not an official source); the official Generalitat 2023 summary (Wayback capture) confirms that separate reserve-place calls ('convocatòria de reserva de places') ran in 2023 for students with disability, Roma students and DGAIA care leavers, with Catalonia-wide counts (assigned via reserve call: disability 364, Roma 14, care leavers 28). The socio-economic vulnerability reserve (1%, IMV / renda garantida recipients) shown on the current Canal Universitats page (updated 30.06.2026) is NOT coded: it is not in the 2023 sources and its start year was not established. The institution's own 2023/24 admission rules were not located (UB/UAB pages not opened; budget). equity_reserved_share_pct 5 = disability only; the Roma and care-leaver reserves are one place per study offer each and are not expressed as a share (not converted). Excluded: elite athletes 3% (5% Fisioteràpia, Educació Primària, CAFE), over-25/40/45, graduates. Filled: Dades_2023 table 7.1 gives new entrants with disability, Roma and care-leaver status; the disability column counts all enrolled students with a disability, which may include some admitted through the general quota (the 2023 summary shows 265 of 629 disabled students Catalonia-wide were assigned in the general call), so equity_filled_entrants is an upper bound on entry under the rule. UB table 7.1 values: Matrícula Discapacitats 204; Poble gitano 0; Tutelats/Extutelats 0; Esportistes 71 (not equity). equity_filled_entrants 204 = 204+0+0. UB lists 87 study offers in table 7.1 (one Roma and one care-leaver reserved place per offer would imply up to 87 each, not entered because the rule's unit 'centre d'estudi' was not verified to equal one row). Cross-check: SIIU (Ministry) reports 11,011 new grado entrants at Universitat de Barcelona for 2023-2024 (different source and definition; not entered).

Of these, 394 were 'international' (secondary diploma obtained abroad; USTAT 07bis, summed by the collector), so domestic-diploma entrants would be 7083 (derived, not entered). Immatricolati exclude anyone previously enrolled at any Italian university (transfers, second degrees, re-enrolments), so first-year enrolment at the institution is larger. sel_unit refers to the entrant headcount (persons); no applicant count was entered. Searches for PoliMi TOL test-taker or applicant counts for 2023/24 returned only third-party estimates (not used); the 2024 Nucleo di Valutazione report (Relazione NdV 2024) was opened and has no applicant counts. Places: the 2023/24 Engineering notice (Art. 7) lists EU places per programme and campus, but the PDF table is linearised and could not be summed reliably; Architecture and Design have separate notices that were not opened; left empty. Regime 'mixed': all Engineering Laurea programmes are programmed by the institution (Senate decision of 23/01/2023 on 'numero programmato'), with its own TOL test (minimum 20 points) and rankings; Architecture is nationally programmed under L. 264/1999 (not verified from a 2023/24 PoliMi document). PoliMi may be closer to own_admission than the other Italian institutions; the coordinator may prefer 'own_admission'. Equity searched: the national framework for 2023/24 entry as cited in the institution's own 2023/24 admission notices (L. 264/1999 on programmed access; L. 104/1992 as amended by L. 17/1999 on disability; L. 170/2010 on specific learning disorders, DSA). These give candidates with disability or DSA extra time and aids in the admission test: an accommodation, not reserved places, bonus points, a lower cutoff or a separate track. The only reserved quotas in the 2023/24 notices opened are for non-EU applicants resident abroad (visa applicants) and Chinese 'Marco Polo' applicants, which are excluded as international quotas. No reservation by income, school type, regional disadvantage or first generation was found. Coded 'no'. Only one or two of the institution's many 2023/24 programme notices were opened, so a programme-specific rule cannot be excluded (equity_confidence medium). PoliMi notice opened: Engineering 2023/24 (copy hosted on ammissione.it of the decree signed 24/01/2023). Its places table reserves places only for non-EU students and Chinese 'Marco Polo' students (and 150 places within Ingegneria informatica for the online programme IOL, not an equity group). Art. 6 gives disability/DSA candidates aids and extra time.

Both counts are tabulated by programme ('por carreras') and summed; the yearbook does not say whether a person applying to two programmes/faculties is counted twice, so the unit is coded 'applications' (conservative). The yearbook gives no definition of 'ingresante'; in UNA usage it is the applicant who passed the faculty admission exam/course and obtained entry. It is entered as `admitted`; a checker may move it to `entrants` (no separate count of enrolled first-year students was found). Pregrado (sub-degree) courses and school-level programmes are in separate tables (3.3.18, 3.3.16) and are excluded. Domestic vs foreign split not stated. Places: not published at institution level; places are set per faculty/programme and some faculties had no cap (Derecho academic director, 2022: 'No existen plazas o cupos para el ingreso'; Medicina 2022: 150 places Asuncion + 40 filial). Regime own_admission: each faculty runs its own entrance exam or probationary admission course (La Nacion 2022 article, nearest year; 2023 faculty admission rules not opened). Equity: yes. Convenio Especifico UNA-INDI (Instituto Paraguayo del Indigena), signed 27 Oct 2020 (date visually checked), 5-year term with automatic renewal, so in force for 2023 entry: UNA reserves places annually through its faculties under a 'Regimen Especial' for indigenous students who completed secondary school; INDI sets the application requirements, selects the candidates and sends the list in February; unfilled places are declared vacant and may be reassigned. Coded basis race_ethnicity (indigenous peoples); instrument reserved_places;separate_track (selection by INDI outside the ordinary exam; a 2026 article by UNA staff calls it 'admision directa'); mandate institutional (agreement between UNA and a government agency; no national law or regulation mandating it was found). The convenio states no share or number of places. 2023 counts: the institution-wide total of places offered under the regime was not found. The ACADEMO 2026 article (Alvarenga Caballero et al., UNA Rectorado staff, from UNA administrative records) gives for 2023 only the four largest units: Instituto Andres Barbero/Enfermeria y Obstetricia 35 places offered (15 'reservadas de forma efectiva por el INDI'), Filosofia 24 (5), FACEN 17 (2), Agrarias 16 (4), i.e. at least 92 offered and 26 taken up by INDI in those four units; not entered because partial and secondary. Over 2008-2023 the article reports 1,249 places offered, 131 reserved by INDI and 94 used; 2023 filled entrants not stated. Not found: any 2023 faculty admission regulation citing the regime; any disability, public-school or income quota in admission (one search on disability reserved places at UNA, no relevant result). Arancel Cero (Ley 6628/2020) waives fees for public-school graduates and vulnerable students; it is financial aid, not an admission rule, and is excluded. WebSearch budget (6 calls) used up.

Unit coded unique_applicants because each UTME candidate names exactly one first-choice institution and the percentage column is a share of all UTME candidates (73,749 = 4.62% for Ilorin implies a base of about 1.6 million, the order of the 2023 UTME candidate total); JAMB's column header says 'applications' - a checker may prefer 'applications'. Scope: UTME candidates only (Direct Entry applicants to 200 level excluded), first choice only, all nationalities (no domestic split; overwhelmingly domestic). Not every first-choice candidate meets the national minimum (140) or the university's own floor. UI 41,134 (10th). admitted/entrants: no 2023/24 count found (the UI matriculation notice for 2023/2024 gives the date, 23 Apr 2024, but no numbers; two searches). Figures found only for 2024/25 (news of the Apr 2025 matriculation: 4,411 UTME + 238 DE admitted; about 22,000 sought admission; 11,912 sat post-UTME) - different year, not entered. places (UI admission quota) not published. Regime mixed: first-degree UTME admission to federal universities runs through JAMB (national UTME exam, national minimum UTME score, admissions proposed by the institution on JAMB's Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS), recommended by the head of institution and approved by JAMB), while the university runs its own post-UTME screening, sets programme cut-offs and makes the admission decisions within its approved quota (JAMB 2024 Policy Meeting deck, slide 'CAPS PROCESS - Reminder', read but not entered as a source row: 'No admission can be initiated from JAMB, .........it must come from the institutions'). Equity YES (national rule): the federal admission guidelines allot first-degree admission places in federal institutions Merit 45%, Catchment 35% and Educationally Less Developed States (ELDS) 20%. Only the ELDS 20% is coded as equity (basis region_or_rural: states designated as educationally disadvantaged); the 35% catchment quota (states near the university) is a locality preference not defined by disadvantage and is NOT counted; merit 45% is not equity. equity_reserved_share_pct = 20 (stated share; the base is the institution's admission quota, which was not found published). Instrument: reserved_places (quota) and lower_cutoff (ELDS candidates are ranked within their own category, so their admitting score can be below the merit cut-off; directly documented only for OAU). Mandate: government_regulation (Federal Government admission guidelines applied through the annual JAMB Policy Meeting chaired by the Minister of Education; not a statute). The document opened with the 45/35/20 shares is the JAMB 2021 Admissions Guidelines (NEAREST YEAR; no 2023 guidelines document found at jamb.gov.ng - the URL pattern 2023_Admission_Guidelines.pdf returns no file); for 2023/2024 the JAMB 2023 Policy Meeting deck ('2023/2024 Admission in Focus: CAPS') states candidates are 'admitted either by Merit, Catchment or ELDS' on CAPS, which confirms the categories for 2023/24 but not the shares - FLAG. The list of ELDS states was not opened from a primary source. Not coded: disability (JAMB 2021 guidelines exempted blind and deaf candidates from post-UTME screening; the 2023 deck only appeals to institutions to admit blind candidates and calls for admission to be 'More inclusive (inclusion of special needs candidates)' - no 2023/24 rule found); the JAMB 2024 deck lists ongoing 2023 admissions of candidates with special needs by institution (counts, not a rule). No count of ELDS entrants published. No UI-specific 2023/24 cut-off list by category (merit/catchment/ELDS) was opened; the undated UI 'Undergraduate Admission Matters' page describes JAMB entry and an O-level/UME aggregate but no quota, so application of the national rule at UI is not directly evidenced. | [K11] checker K11 reads ELDS (whole-state eligibility) as territorial under D071; kept yes pending investigator

adm_notes: University of Lagos. applicants = JAMB 2023 UTME first-choice applications for the institution (JAMB Registrar's Report to the 2023 Policy Meeting, 24 Jun 2023, slide 'Top Ten Institutions - All Universities (First Choice)', read from the rendered page). Unit coded unique_applicants because each UTME candidate names exactly one first-choice institution and the percentage column is a share of all UTME candidates (73,749 = 4.62% for Ilorin implies a base of about 1.6 million, the order of the 2023 UTME candidate total); JAMB's column header says 'applications' - a checker may prefer 'applications'. Scope: UTME candidates only (Direct Entry applicants to 200 level excluded), first choice only, all nationalities (no domestic split; overwhelmingly domestic). Not every first-choice candidate meets the national minimum (140) or the university's own floor. UNILAG 61,606 (2nd). CONFLICT kept: a BusinessDay article (May 2026, read via WebFetch) gives 60,606 for UNILAG in 2023; the JAMB slide (primary, visually read) gives 61,606 and is used. entrants = 8,448 'formally admitted to the studentship' at the 2 Feb 2024 matriculation for the 'merged 2022/2023 and 2023/2024 academic sessions', which 'formally ends the admission process for the 2023/2024 Academic Session' (UNILAG official news). UNILAG's own applicant figure in the same text, 'over fifty-three thousand (53,000) that applied', is a lower bound and is not entered; it differs from JAMB's 61,606 first-choice count (UNILAG's figure may count only candidates who applied for post-UTME screening; not stated). SCOPE FLAG: entrants may include Direct Entry while applicants are UTME-only. admitted (offers) and places (admission quota) not published. Regime mixed: first-degree UTME admission to federal universities runs through JAMB (national UTME exam, national minimum UTME score, admissions proposed by the institution on JAMB's Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS), recommended by the head of institution and approved by JAMB), while the university runs its own post-UTME screening, sets programme cut-offs and makes the admission decisions within its approved quota (JAMB 2024 Policy Meeting deck, slide 'CAPS PROCESS - Reminder', read but not entered as a source row: 'No admission can be initiated from JAMB, .........it must come from the institutions'). Equity YES (national rule): the federal admission guidelines allot first-degree admission places in federal institutions Merit 45%, Catchment 35% and Educationally Less Developed States (ELDS) 20%. Only the ELDS 20% is coded as equity (basis region_or_rural: states designated as educationally disadvantaged); the 35% catchment quota (states near the university) is a locality preference not defined by disadvantage and is NOT counted; merit 45% is not equity. equity_reserved_share_pct = 20 (stated share; the base is the institution's admission quota, which was not found published). Instrument: reserved_places (quota) and lower_cutoff (ELDS candidates are ranked within their own category, so their admitting score can be below the merit cut-off; directly documented only for OAU). Mandate: government_regulation (Federal Government admission guidelines applied through the annual JAMB Policy Meeting chaired by the Minister of Education; not a statute). The document opened with the 45/35/20 shares is the JAMB 2021 Admissions Guidelines (NEAREST YEAR; no 2023 guidelines document found at jamb.gov.ng - the URL pattern 2023_Admission_Guidelines.pdf returns no file); for 2023/2024 the JAMB 2023 Policy Meeting deck ('2023/2024 Admission in Focus: CAPS') states candidates are 'admitted either by Merit, Catchment or ELDS' on CAPS, which confirms the categories for 2023/24 but not the shares - FLAG. The list of ELDS states was not opened from a primary source. Not coded: disability (JAMB 2021 guidelines exempted blind and deaf candidates from post-UTME screening; the 2023 deck only appeals to institutions to admit blind candidates and calls for admission to be 'More inclusive (inclusion of special needs candidates)' - no 2023/24 rule found); the JAMB 2024 deck lists ongoing 2023 admissions of candidates with special needs by institution (counts, not a rule). No count of ELDS entrants published. UNILAG's own 2023/24 notice (15 Sep 2023) publishes 'UTME Merit Cut-Off Marks', implying separate non-merit categories, but the catchment/ELDS cut-offs and the linked list were not obtained; application of the rule at UNILAG is not directly evidenced. Secondary sites state a UNILAG split Merit 40 or 45%, Catchment 35%, ELDS 20% - not used. | [K11] checker K11 reads ELDS (whole-state eligibility) as territorial under D071; kept yes pending investigator

adm_notes: Selectivity: Portuguese public universities fill first-degree (licenciatura and integrated master's) places through the Concurso Nacional de Acesso (CNA) run by DGES, which ranks candidates by score across up to six ordered institution/programme preferences: central_allocation. All figures are for the 2023 CNA, 1st phase, summed in code over the 56 institution/programme pairs of Universidade do Porto (14 DGES establishment codes; all schools and campuses) in the DGES StatsEstab23.pdf per-programme table (parsed with pdftotext -raw; new 2023 programmes with no 2022 row handled separately) and cross-checked against the DGES 1st-phase xlsx (places identical programme by programme). places = CNA 1st-phase initial places (4706); they include the priority-contingent places carved out of each programme's places and exclude places of special contests (over-23, international students, holders of other degrees, transfers) and of the 2nd/3rd phases. applicants = 26544 applications ('Candidatos Total' = candidates who listed the programme in any preference, summed over programmes, so a person who listed two programmes of the institution counts twice); unique applicants are not published at institution level. Candidates with one of the institution's programmes as FIRST option = 7576 (persons, first preference only; not entered). admitted = 4635 1st-phase placements (colocados, all contingents; = xlsx Colocados 4628 + ties (desemp.) 5 + placed without final secondary grade 2); 2nd- and 3rd-phase placements not added (they partly re-place candidates already placed). entrants = 4643 = InfoCursos June-2024 database (DGEEC), sheet 'Percentil Entrada', column NumeroMatriculadosCNA2023, summed over the institution's programmes: students who enrolled through the 2023 CNA (the technical note describes them only as 'alunos que entraram pelo CNA'; presumably all three phases). It excludes special-contest and special-regime entrants, so it is not total first-year intake. Cross-check: U.Porto news (27.08.23) states 4,706 places, 4,635 placed and 7,576 first-option candidates for 56 programmes, matching the DGES-derived figures. Rates not computed here. DGEEC 'Vagas e inscritos pela 1.ª vez no Ensino Superior 2023/2024' (Info DGEEC N.º 9) has an institution/programme table of first-time first-year enrolments by entry route, but its file link could not be located (flipbook page); not used. Equity: Portaria n.º 104/2023 (Regulamento do Concurso Nacional de Acesso for 2023-2024, ministerial regulation under DL 296-A/98 art. 28) art. 10(3) creates priority contingents in the CNA 1st phase: (e) candidates with disability, the larger of 4% of 1st-phase places or two places (and 2% or one place in the 2nd phase); (f) beneficiaries of school social action (ação social escolar, ASE: escalão A in the last year of secondary school, or Azores escalões I/II; income-tested), 2% of 1st-phase places or two places (described by DGES as new in 2023). Candidates not placed in a contingent compete in the general contingent (art. 10(6)). Excluded from the equity coding and flagged for the checker: the contingents for candidates from the Autonomous Regions of the Azores (3.5%) and Madeira (3.5%) (defined by regional origin/residence; the regulation does not state disadvantage), emigrants and luso-descendants (7%), and military (2.5%). Per DGES's 2023 ASE page all programmes of all public institutions in the 2023 CNA have the ASE contingent except IPVC, ULisboa and NOVA, so both contingents apply to all of this institution's CNA programmes. equity_reserved_share_pct = 6 = 4 (disability) + 2 (ASE), as stated per programme for the 1st phase; the two-place minimum per contingent and rounding (art. 10(4)) make the effective share higher in small programmes. Reserved place counts were not found as a published institution total and were not computed. Filled: DGES StCEs23.pdf (1st phase, one page per programme, table 'ETAPA COLOCAÇÃO (contingente)', column Cols.) summed in code over the institution's programme pages: Deficientes 18 + ASE 94 = 112 placements; base = all 1st-phase placements 4635 (stage sums reconcile exactly: Geral 4293, Açores 68, Madeira 80, Emigrantes 79, Militares 3). These are placements, not enrolments; 2nd-phase disability placements not added. No institution-specific admission regulation beyond the national CNA rules was opened; access to these programmes is governed by the CNA regulation.

adm_notes: Selectivity: Portuguese public universities fill first-degree (licenciatura and integrated master's) places through the Concurso Nacional de Acesso (CNA) run by DGES, which ranks candidates by score across up to six ordered institution/programme preferences: central_allocation. All figures are for the 2023 CNA, 1st phase, summed in code over the 42 institution/programme pairs of Universidade Nova de Lisboa (6 DGES establishment codes; all schools and campuses) in the DGES StatsEstab23.pdf per-programme table (parsed with pdftotext -raw; new 2023 programmes with no 2022 row handled separately) and cross-checked against the DGES 1st-phase xlsx (places identical programme by programme). places = CNA 1st-phase initial places (2821); they include the priority-contingent places carved out of each programme's places and exclude places of special contests (over-23, international students, holders of other degrees, transfers) and of the 2nd/3rd phases. applicants = 18323 applications ('Candidatos Total' = candidates who listed the programme in any preference, summed over programmes, so a person who listed two programmes of the institution counts twice); unique applicants are not published at institution level. Candidates with one of the institution's programmes as FIRST option = 4363 (persons, first preference only; not entered). admitted = 2777 1st-phase placements (colocados, all contingents; = xlsx Colocados 2763 + ties (desemp.) 2 + placed without final secondary grade 12); 2nd- and 3rd-phase placements not added (they partly re-place candidates already placed). entrants = 2804 = InfoCursos June-2024 database (DGEEC), sheet 'Percentil Entrada', column NumeroMatriculadosCNA2023, summed over the institution's programmes: students who enrolled through the 2023 CNA (the technical note describes them only as 'alunos que entraram pelo CNA'; presumably all three phases). It excludes special-contest and special-regime entrants, so it is not total first-year intake. Rates not computed here. DGEEC 'Vagas e inscritos pela 1.ª vez no Ensino Superior 2023/2024' (Info DGEEC N.º 9) has an institution/programme table of first-time first-year enrolments by entry route, but its file link could not be located (flipbook page); not used. Equity: Portaria n.º 104/2023 (Regulamento do Concurso Nacional de Acesso for 2023-2024, ministerial regulation under DL 296-A/98 art. 28) art. 10(3) creates priority contingents in the CNA 1st phase: (e) candidates with disability, the larger of 4% of 1st-phase places or two places (and 2% or one place in the 2nd phase); (f) beneficiaries of school social action (ação social escolar, ASE: escalão A in the last year of secondary school, or Azores escalões I/II; income-tested), 2% of 1st-phase places or two places (described by DGES as new in 2023). Candidates not placed in a contingent compete in the general contingent (art. 10(6)). Excluded from the equity coding and flagged for the checker: the contingents for candidates from the Autonomous Regions of the Azores (3.5%) and Madeira (3.5%) (defined by regional origin/residence; the regulation does not state disadvantage), emigrants and luso-descendants (7%), and military (2.5%). Institution-specific: per DGES's 2023 ASE page, Universidade Nova de Lisboa set ASE places only for some programmes in 2023: 16 of 42 CNA programmes (DGES list escalaoa_unl.xlsx: Ciências da Nutrição, Medicina (FCM/NMS); Bioquímica, Engenharia Civil, Engenharia de Materiais, Engenharia Geológica, Engenharia Química e Biológica, Biologia Celular e Molecular, Engenharia de Micro e Nanotecnologias, Tecnologia Agro-Industrial (FCT); Economia, Gestão (Faculdade de Economia/SBE); Sistemas e Tecnologias de Informação, Gestão de Informação, Ciência de Dados (IMS); Direito (FD)); no FCSH programme; 14 of them had ASE candidates. The disability contingent applies to all programmes. So equity_scope = all_programmes refers to the disability contingent; the income (ASE) contingent is some_programmes. The legal basis for this institutional limitation is not stated in Portaria 104/2023 (which creates the contingent without exception); flagged. equity_reserved_share_pct = 4 (disability, as stated) only; the ASE 2% applies only to the listed programmes and no institution-wide reserved share is stated. Reserved place counts were not found as a published institution total and were not computed. Filled: DGES StCEs23.pdf (1st phase, one page per programme, table 'ETAPA COLOCAÇÃO (contingente)', column Cols.) summed in code over the institution's programme pages: Deficientes 15 + ASE 23 = 38 placements; base = all 1st-phase placements 2777 (stage sums reconcile exactly: Geral 2598, Açores 37, Madeira 40, Emigrantes 61, Militares 3). These are placements, not enrolments; 2nd-phase disability placements not added. No institution-specific admission regulation beyond the national CNA rules was opened; access to these programmes is governed by the CNA regulation.

notes: Control public: listed as 'Uczelnia publiczna' supervised by the science minister in the official POL-on/RAD-on register; PSWN art. 13(1)(1) defines a public university as one created by a state organ and art. 35(1) creates public academic universities by statute. Under the strict test note that the rada uczelni is appointed by the university senate (art. 19), not by the state, and the rector is elected, so 'public' rests on state foundation/ownership, not on a state-appointed board. Tuition 0: Constitution art. 70(2) and PSWN art. 79(1) allow fees only for part-time, repeated, foreign-language, extra-curricular classes and foreigners; the institution's 2023/24 fee regulation sets no fee for Polish-citizen full-time Polish-language study (rule application plus absence in the schedule). Fee-paying tracks in the 2023/24 regulation: part-time (e.g. administracja niestacjonarne first cycle 5,000 zł/yr single payment), foreign-language programmes, repeats and extra classes. Fees 0: the only other permitted charges (art. 79(2)) are recruitment (85 zł, application fee, excluded), the one-off 22 zł electronic student ID at issue (excluded as one-off per project precedent; no band effect), duplicates and dormitories/canteens; art. 80(6) bars other document fees; no recurring compulsory fee found. Govt targeted: stypendium socjalne is tested on per-person family income (student, spouse, parents) against a threshold set by the rector within statutory limits (art. 87-88), paid from the university's Fundusz Stypendialny, which is funded by a ministerial grant (art. 365 pkt 3, 366, 412) and administered by the university, so coded government-funded; nationally 52.4k of 1,245.2k students (about 4.2%, derived) received it in 2023/24; zapomoga (hardship grant) is from the same fund; state-guaranteed student loans excluded. Inst unknown: no UW-run means-tested scheme found in a limited search; UW's own 2025 page says social aid is paid from the Ministry-funded Fundusz Stypendialny; PSWN art. 420 limits a university's own scholarship fund to merit awards; the Fundacja UW is a separate legal body (D036, not counted). | [V012] Ownership evidence: PSWN art. 423(2) applies the State Property Management Act 2016 (consent of the Prokuratoria Generalna) to a public university's disposal of fixed assets above 2 million zł, and on liquidation a minister-appointed liquidator takes over the university organs (art. 36). adm_notes: REGIME central_allocation: under the MON Admission Procedure 2023 (order No 276) applicants apply electronically through EDEBO (up to 5 applications for state-funded places and 20 in total); state-funded (budget) places on open competitive offers are allocated by 'адресне розміщення бюджетних місць' computed in EDEBO from the NMT-based competitive score and applicants' priorities within national 'широкі конкурси'; the institution sets contract (fee-paying) intake within its licence and ranks contract applicants by the same nationally defined competitive score (arguably mixed for the contract track). SELECTIVITY: applicants is a sum computed here (15831 bachelor ПЗСО + 166 integrated master ПЗСО) of two stated values on the vstup.osvita.ua institution page (Wayback capture 2024-11-15; 'Дані отримані з ЄДЕБО 01.12.2023'); unit = applications (one person may file up to 20, of which 5 for budget places), not unique applicants. places = 3740 + 60 = maximum state-order volume (budget places) from the same page - NOT total capacity: the licence volume (ліцензійний обсяг) for ПЗСО entry was 7849 bachelor + 94 integrated, and contract intake is set by the institution within the licence. entrants 5134 from EDEBO official open data (generated 01.01.2026) differ slightly from the vstup.osvita snapshot of 01.12.2023 (bachelor 2740 budget + 2251 contract = 4991; integrated 53 + 6); the EDEBO figure is used. Admitted (recommendations/offers) not published at institution level. Bachelor entry after junior-specialist/НРК5 diplomas (shortened, often into year 2-3) excluded. Cross-check: abit-poisk.org.ua 2023 sums for KNU full-time ПЗСО bachelor offers give 29296 applications (about 1.8x the vstup.osvita figure) with nearly identical budget places (3748), so application counts differ by aggregator definition; not used. EQUITY yes (national rule, applied in the institution's 2023 rules): two reserved shares of STATE-FUNDED places for first-degree entry on the basis of complete secondary school (ПЗСО) or НРК5. Quota-1 (квота-1): set by the institution 'within ten percent (but not less than one place)' of the maximum/total state-order volume of open and fixed competitive offers; eligible: orphans and children deprived of parental care (basis other), persons with disabilities/medical conditions preventing NMT participation (basis disability), persons deprived of liberty due to the armed aggression (other), and also combat participants/Revolution of Dignity victims (service-related, not an equity group under this protocol, but sharing the same quota). Quota-2 (квота-2): residents of temporarily occupied territories, front-line/active-combat settlements or areas de-occupied after 24.02.2022, and those who moved from them (basis region_or_rural: war-affected region of residence). Quota applicants compete among themselves for the quota places ahead of the general list; if not recommended they compete on general conditions. Instrument reserved_places. equity_reserved_share_pct is the SUM of the stated shares: quota-1 is a ceiling ('в межах'), so the actual quota-1 share is <= the stated value and may include non-equity (veteran) applicants; quotas are shares of state-funded places only, not of all (incl. contract) places. Counts of quota places and of entrants admitted under the quotas are published only per competitive offer (rating lists flag quota applicants, e.g. 'КВ2'); no institution-level total was found, so equity_reserved_places and equity_filled_entrants are empty (not published at institution level). Not coded as equity: transfer to vacant state-funded places (розділ VIII пп.10-11) for IDPs, children from families with 5+ children, disabled persons etc. already enrolled on contract (a funding-transfer priority, not an admission rule); the regional coefficient RK (depends on the institution's location, not the applicant's); priority admission for applicants signing a rural service agreement (service obligation); quotas for foreigners. Mandate: Law 1556-VII art. 44(3) provides quota admission for orphans, persons with conditions preventing external testing, combatants and residents of occupied territory (consolidated text; para 3 reworded 21.11.2023); MON order No 276 sets the shares; institution rules apply them. Institution: KNU 2023 rules (general provisions p.6 and §4.1.2) state both quota-1 and quota-2 'у межах десяти відсотків' (KNU wording for quota-2; the national text after order 682 says 'в обсязі' 10%; Kyiv city is not in the 40% list): sum 20. Base 3800 = maximum state order for ПЗСО bachelor + integrated entry (vstup.osvita snapshot); the rule applies per competitive offer, so 20% x 3800 is not a published count. For reference only (not entered): abit-poisk.org.ua 2023 offer lists for Karazin sum (computed here) to 1571 budget places (BM, max) and 9535 applications for full-time ПЗСО bachelor offers, 21 BM / 1447 applications for extramural ПЗСО bachelor offers, and 107 BM / 399 applications for integrated master ПЗСО offers; abit-poisk application counts are about 1.8x the vstup.osvita counts for KNU and Lviv Polytechnic, so their definition differs. entrants 2734 from EDEBO official open data (generated 01.01.2026). Admitted not published. EQUITY yes (national rule, applied in the institution's 2023 rules): two reserved shares of STATE-FUNDED places for first-degree entry on the basis of complete secondary school (ПЗСО) or НРК5. Quota-1 (квота-1): set by the institution 'within ten percent (but not less than one place)' of the maximum/total state-order volume of open and fixed competitive offers; eligible: orphans and children deprived of parental care (basis other), persons with disabilities/medical conditions preventing NMT participation (basis disability), persons deprived of liberty due to the armed aggression (other), and also combat participants/Revolution of Dignity victims (service-related, not an equity group under this protocol, but sharing the same quota). Quota-2 (квота-2): residents of temporarily occupied territories, front-line/active-combat settlements or areas de-occupied after 24.02.2022, and those who moved from them (basis region_or_rural: war-affected region of residence). Quota applicants compete among themselves for the quota places ahead of the general list; if not recommended they compete on general conditions. Instrument reserved_places. equity_reserved_share_pct is the SUM of the stated shares: quota-1 is a ceiling ('в межах'), so the actual quota-1 share is <= the stated value and may include non-equity (veteran) applicants; quotas are shares of state-funded places only, not of all (incl. contract) places. Counts of quota places and of entrants admitted under the quotas are published only per competitive offer (rating lists flag quota applicants, e.g. 'КВ2'); no institution-level total was found, so equity_reserved_places and equity_filled_entrants are empty (not published at institution level). Not coded as equity: transfer to vacant state-funded places (розділ VIII пп.10-11) for IDPs, children from families with 5+ children, disabled persons etc. already enrolled on contract (a funding-transfer priority, not an admission rule); the regional coefficient RK (depends on the institution's location, not the applicant's); priority admission for applicants signing a rural service agreement (service obligation); quotas for foreigners. Mandate: Law 1556-VII art. 44(3) provides quota admission for orphans, persons with conditions preventing external testing, combatants and residents of occupied territory (consolidated text; para 3 reworded 21.11.2023); MON order No 276 sets the shares; institution rules apply them. Institution: Karazin 2023 rules (amended 07.07.2023) reproduce the national quota-1 and quota-2 eligibility lists (розділ VIII пп.7-8) and state that quota volumes are published on the university website; the percentage is not restated in the passages read. Share: Karazin is a Kharkiv-oblast HEI, so under розділ XV п.12 of the national Procedure (wording of order 682 of 06.06.2023) quota-2 is 40% of the maximum/total state order, plus quota-1 up to 10%: stated sum 50 (application of the national rule to the institution's location; institution-level quota counts not found).

Tuition 0: full-time EU-citizen students at public HEIs have tuition fully subsidised by the state (art. 79; Uredba NN 78/2023 art. 5(3)) when enrolling in first year for the first time or with >=55 ECTS in the prior year; students below 55 ECTS pay pro-rata participation (FFZG max 955.60 EUR); foreign-language programmes and second same-level qualifications are not covered (outside the headline). Fees: each of the ~30 constituent faculties sets its own enrolment charge; only two 2023/24 schedules were opened: FFZG first-year undergraduate package 35.84 EUR and EFZG upisnina 66.36 EUR (bundles accident insurance, publishing, SmartX card, e-Indeks); headline = midpoint of this 2-faculty sample; the true range across faculties is not established. notes: Control public: state HEI, legal form viesoji istaiga, owner the Lithuanian state (statute approved by Seimas law, art. 2); the law says the state owns every state university and bars private or public co-owners (art. 34(2)). The council (taryba) is not state-appointed: 5 members elected by academics, 4 external members elected under Senate rules, 2 chosen by students. Public on ownership. Headline: VU 2023-2024 fee schedule (Senate decision SPN-10, 21 Feb 2023), column 'VU metine', full-time (NL) first-cycle and integrated programmes: min 2865 (e.g. Filosofija, Istorija, Kriminologija, Sociologija, Anglų ir kita užsienio (ispanų) kalba (business programmes are 3060 in the VU column)) to max 9000 (Odontology, integrated, normative 8244); midpoint 5932.5. Without Odontology the max would be 6600 (Medicine). Maximum read visually from the rendered page, minimum machine-extracted from the price column. Law rows for applicants who already hold a degree are excluded (second degree). No recurring compulsory fee found (not separately verified). Confidence medium only because of the institutional-aid evidence; the charge evidence is official and for 2023-24. Split subsidy track (D038): admission to state-funded places (valstybes finansuojamos vietos, VF) is by competitive admission score and VF students pay no study-related charges to a state HEI (Law on Higher Education and Research art. 83(5)); VF funding is kept only while the student meets the good-performance criteria, and a lost VF place passes to the best VNF student (art. 78(5)). The headline is the price actually paid on non-state-funded (VNF) places. Share of first-year students on VF places not established (not required by D038). Govt targeted: state social scholarship (socialine stipendija, 6.5 BSI = 318.50 EUR/month in 2023, paid by Valstybinis studiju fondas) for students on VF or VNF places whose household is entitled to the means-tested social assistance benefit (socialine pasalpa); the other two eligibility routes (disability, orphanhood) are not means-tested. Eligibility is tied to the social-assistance threshold, so coverage is narrow; recipient share not found. National scheme cited by rule. adm_notes: REGIME central_allocation: domestic first-cycle and integrated entry runs through the national centralised admission (bendrasis priemimas) operated by LAMA BPO on the ministry's mandate: applicants list up to 9 ranked preferences and are allocated by competitive score; state-funded places are distributed by study-field group across institutions by ministerial order (LAMA BPO 2023 description pt 43). Institutions set their own score rules and capacity only for non-state-funded places, and admit most third-country nationals directly outside the central system (LAMA BPO 2023 review p.4: up to 90% of all students are admitted centrally). Final central results fixed 31 Aug 2023 (main stage + two additional stages). SELECTIVITY: applicants 32452 is a sum computed here (28163 + 4289) of two stated chart values (VU annual report 2023, p.37, diagram 23, visually checked); unit is applications = ranked preferences across all priorities (the report says 48.4% of all preferences were 1st or 2nd priority), so one person counts several times; includes foreign applications (>2,500 across all levels, not split by level). Unique applicants to VU not published. Admitted (invitations) not found. entrants 4772 is stated in the text (p.41) and equals 4094 bachelor + 678 integrated (diagram 28). CONFLICT: VU attributes 4,772 to 'LAMA BPO duomenimis', but the LAMA BPO 2023 review table 7 gives VU 3,533 state-funded/stipend + 693 non-funded contracts = 4,226 (sum computed here) in central admission; the difference (546) is plausibly direct/international admission but this is not stated - checker should decide which figure to use (the LAMA figure is the central-admission scope used for LTU-MR and LTU-VM). PLACES: empty. State-funded places are set by the ministry per study-field group nationally (12,767 incl. stipend places, 8,700 for universities in 2023 per LAMA review table 1), not per institution; no institution-level total of first-year places was found for 2023. EQUITY: no. For 2023 entry the national ranking rule (ministerial KE aprasas 2023, order V-1901 of 30 Nov 2022, applied through CP aprasas V-329 of 14 Mar 2023) gave additional points only for olympiad/competition prizes, maturity project grade, diaspora Lithuanians (foreign-resident Lithuanians/Lithuanian-origin foreigners), VET with distinction, basic military training/service and volunteering (as reproduced in VU's 2023 methodology pt 14) - merit, diaspora and service criteria, none defined by disadvantage. The LAMA BPO 2023 centralised admission description contains no second competitive queue or reserved share (the string 'antr' does not occur in it); a second competitive queue receiving up to 10% of state-funded places, open inter alia to social-benefit recipients, persons with disability and orphans/former wards, appears in the 2024 description (pt 49), i.e. from 2024 entry, outside the reference year. The KE aprasas 2023 itself (e-tar.lt) returned HTTP 403 and was not read directly; its content is taken from institutional rules that reproduce it. Fee waivers (application/registration fee) for social-benefit recipients, disabled persons and orphans exist at several institutions but are financial, not admission rules. VU 2023 methodology (pts 14-16) lists national and VU-own additional points (olympiads, diaspora, military service, volunteering, VU schools/courses) and tie-break order (exam scores, priority, Lithuanian exam) - no disadvantage criterion. VU's general 2023 admission rules document was not opened separately.

adm_notes: Selectivity: places and entrants from MOE institutional-research table 學12-2 for 112學年度 (2023/24), day bachelor row (quoted with columns B, D and E). Overseas/foreign new entrants (column D) are reported separately and not added. Applicants and admitted: not published institution-wide in the sources opened; sel_unit left empty because no applicant count is recorded. Taiwan first-degree entry runs through several channels: 繁星推薦 (school-recommendation route allocated centrally by CAC), 申請入學/個人申請 (two stages: CAC first-stage screening on GSAT scores, then the university's own second-stage review and decision, followed by CAC unified allocation; candidates may apply to several programmes), 分發入學 (central score-based allocation by UAC) and 特殊選才 (own admission). No source opened gives unique applicants across channels; per-programme application counts exist for the 個人申請 channel only (e.g. NTU's 112 申請入學錄取情況 PDF; applications, not unique persons; no total row) and were not summed. Regime coded mixed (central allocation for 繁星/分發 plus institution-decided second stage in 個人申請 and own 特殊選才); the regime description rests on the channel documents opened plus general knowledge of the system - FLAG for the checker (no single official regime statement was quoted). Equity: YES. Institutional: NTU 希望組 (Hope groups), 8 groups in the 112 申請入學 channel with their own places (甲12, 乙3, 丙6, 丁8, 戊13, 己4, 庚9, 辛2 = 57 per CAC's 112 screening-standard table; total computed by the collector from 8 stated cells - checker to verify), open only to students from households certified as low-income or middle-low-income in 2023, certified special-circumstance families, children of new immigrants (新住民子女, coded other), or students who attended remote-area (偏遠地區) high schools for all three years (coded region_or_rural) -> separate_track. equity_reserved_places = 57 (希望組 only); base = NTU day-bachelor within-quota approved places 3,467 (MOE 學12-2), assuming 希望組 places sit within the approved quota (not stated explicitly; FLAG). Not counted: NTU's separate 希望入學 independent admission (獨招) for disadvantaged students (seen only in search-result titles, not opened; places unknown); per-programme indigenous supernumerary places (NTU's 112 須知 refers to programmes listing '原住民外加名額'; counts not extracted). Filled: 希望組 admissions per group appear in NTU's 112 申請入學錄取情況 PDF (admitted after allocation, not registered entrants; no total) - equity_filled_entrants not published in sources opened. National rule (applies to all five): 原住民學生升學保障及原住民公費留學辦法 (MOE regulation issued under 原住民族教育法 art. 23; current version amended 2019-12-18, in force for 2023/24) gives indigenous applicants supernumerary places (外加名額) of 2% of the approved places (rounded up; may be exceeded for ties and by special decision) and, in the exam-allocation route (分發入學), a bonus of 10% of the raw total score (35% with an indigenous culture and language certificate); in other routes universities may give consideration. Coded reserved_places (supernumerary) + bonus_points; basis race_ethnicity; mandate national_law;government_regulation. equity_reserved_share_pct = 2 is the stated indigenous supernumerary share only (added on top of the approved places, not inside them); the institutional disadvantaged tracks have no stated share, so the 2 is NOT a sum over categories. Disability: a national separate examination track exists (身心障礙學生升學大專校院甄試; 112 university-group registration statistics published on cis.ncu.edu.tw), but institution-level participation and places for 112 were not found in sources opened; disability is coded only where the institution's own track names it. equity_scope all_programmes because the indigenous national rule covers every programme; the institutional tracks cover named groups of programmes in the 申請入學 channel.

adm_notes: Selectivity: places and entrants from MOE institutional-research table 學12-2 for 112學年度 (2023/24), day bachelor row (quoted with columns B, D and E). Overseas/foreign new entrants (column D) are reported separately and not added. Applicants and admitted: not published institution-wide in the sources opened; sel_unit left empty because no applicant count is recorded. Taiwan first-degree entry runs through several channels: 繁星推薦 (school-recommendation route allocated centrally by CAC), 申請入學/個人申請 (two stages: CAC first-stage screening on GSAT scores, then the university's own second-stage review and decision, followed by CAC unified allocation; candidates may apply to several programmes), 分發入學 (central score-based allocation by UAC) and 特殊選才 (own admission). No source opened gives unique applicants across channels; per-programme application counts exist for the 個人申請 channel only (e.g. NTU's 112 申請入學錄取情況 PDF; applications, not unique persons; no total row) and were not summed. Regime coded mixed (central allocation for 繁星/分發 plus institution-decided second stage in 個人申請 and own 特殊選才); the regime description rests on the channel documents opened plus general knowledge of the system - FLAG for the checker (no single official regime statement was quoted). Equity: YES. Institutional: NYCU 屯蒙 groups in the 112 申請入學 channel (9 groups: 電機資訊25, 工程14, 理學生物科技13, 管理9, 人文社會6, 醫學2, 牙醫2, 醫事證照5, 生醫科學3 = 79 places per CAC's 112 screening-standard table; total computed by the collector), restricted to disadvantaged applicants: economically disadvantaged (low-income, middle-low-income, special-circumstance), new immigrants and their children (coded other), students with disabilities and children of persons with disabilities, and indigenous applicants (NYCU 112 校系分則, Wayback capture 2023-06-27; live file now 404) -> separate_track. Many departments also give priority admission within quota to low/middle-low-income candidates ('至多N名'; no total stated). equity_reserved_places = 79 (屯蒙 only); base = NYCU day-bachelor within-quota approved places 1,738 (MOE 學12-2; within-quota assumption FLAG). Filled entrants not published in sources opened. National rule (applies to all five): 原住民學生升學保障及原住民公費留學辦法 (MOE regulation issued under 原住民族教育法 art. 23; current version amended 2019-12-18, in force for 2023/24) gives indigenous applicants supernumerary places (外加名額) of 2% of the approved places (rounded up; may be exceeded for ties and by special decision) and, in the exam-allocation route (分發入學), a bonus of 10% of the raw total score (35% with an indigenous culture and language certificate); in other routes universities may give consideration. Coded reserved_places (supernumerary) + bonus_points; basis race_ethnicity; mandate national_law;government_regulation. equity_reserved_share_pct = 2 is the stated indigenous supernumerary share only (added on top of the approved places, not inside them); the institutional disadvantaged tracks have no stated share, so the 2 is NOT a sum over categories. Disability: a national separate examination track exists (身心障礙學生升學大專校院甄試; 112 university-group registration statistics published on cis.ncu.edu.tw), but institution-level participation and places for 112 were not found in sources opened; disability is coded only where the institution's own track names it. equity_scope all_programmes because the indigenous national rule covers every programme; the institutional tracks cover named groups of programmes in the 申請入學 channel.

The childcare-leave points (c) are not coded as a disadvantage basis (life situation, not a disadvantage group); recorded here only. All bonus points together are capped at 100 under the Decree ('A (3) bekezdés c)–f) pontja alapján adható többletpontok összege legfeljebb 100 pont lehet', same time state, 15. § (4)). No places are reserved, so reserved share/places are empty (not applicable). Filled counts (admitted or entrants who received equity bonus points) were not found at institution level in the sources opened (felvi.hu institution statistics are in a Power BI dashboard not readable here; the institutional reports opened do not report them) - not_published/unknown. Institutional admission regulations for 2023 were not opened individually - gap; for 2023 first-degree entry the point calculation was set nationally by the Decree.

Sport aptitude 412 / 296 / 150. Equity: no. National law (UG 2002 as of 01.09.2023): § 71b(7) requires admission procedures to use performance-related criteria, to ensure no discrimination by gender or social origin (Z 2), and gives applicants with a disability the right to request a different examination method (Z 5) - an accommodation, not a reservation, bonus, lower threshold or separate track; § 71c(5) reserves 75% of human-medicine places for holders of Austrian school-leaving certificates and 95% for EU citizens (certificate origin/nationality, not disadvantage; human medicine is taught at the separate medical universities, not here). The minister appoints all members of the správní rada (§ 14(1)), a supervisory body, not the governing body; the academic senate is elected by the academic community and the rector is appointed by the President on the senate's proposal (§ 10(2)), so 'public' rests on state ownership, not on a state-appointed governing majority (same reading as the other CZE rows; national rule applied). adm_notes: National framework: Act 111/1998 Coll. (consolidated text in force 2026, verze 46, read at zakonyprolidi.cz; the 2023 wording was not separately opened) lets the university/faculty set admission conditions on knowledge, abilities, talent or school results and a maximum intake, with ranking of the best when more applicants qualify (§ 49(1)); different conditions are allowed only for applicants with prior HE/VOŠ study and for government development-scholarship holders (§ 49(3)); no provision reserves places, adds points, lowers thresholds or opens a track for a disadvantage-defined group. Applicants apply directly to the faculty (or university) and the dean (or rector) decides (§ 50(1)-(2)), hence own_admission. Places: § 49(5) requires each programme's maximum intake to be published on the institution's or faculty's web pages; no institution-level sum of places for 2023/24 was found, so places is empty. Selectivity unit: the MŠMT-mandated annual-report table ('Zájem o studium na vysoké škole') gives, per degree type, 'Počet uchazečů' (applicants, counted once per degree type), 'Počet přihlášek' (applications), 'Počet přijatých' (admitted) and 'Počet zapsaných' (enrolled). First-degree = Bc. (bachelor) + Mgr. (long-cycle master not following a bachelor). Entered: applications, admitted and enrolled summed over these two types (unit applications); unique applicants per type are given in the notes but not summed into the applicants field because a person can be counted in both types. Calendar 2023 admissions = 2023/24 entry; all applicants, domestic and foreign (no domestic split); all forms of study (full-time and combined/distance). UPOL values (annual report on activities 2023, Tabulková příloha, Tab. 5.1 část 2a, row 'UP CELKEM', appendix p. 24 of 48; checked visually on the rendered page): Bakalářské studium Počet uchazečů (fyzické osoby) 14062, přihlášek 21702, přijetí 6474, zápisů ke studiu 4896; Magisterské (long-cycle) studium uchazečů 6282, přihlášek 7403, přijetí 1597, zápisů 1008. Entered: applications 21702+7403=29105; admitted 6474+1597=8071; entrants 4896+1008=5904. Unique applicants per type summed would be 20344 (not entered). Cross-checks: the UP CELKEM Mgr. applications/admitted/enrolled equal the sums of the ISCED rows (researcher's addition); the report text gives 25 779 applicants and 35 722 applications for all degree types and, in a chart, 11 354 applicants and 13 633 applications for long-cycle + follow-up master's combined (7403 + 6230 = 13633). Data-quality flag: in the same table the faculty block 'PřF celkem' repeats its Bc. values in the Magisterské columns (3061/4025/1738/1336), apparently a template error; the UP CELKEM Mgr. values do not include these figures (they match the ISCED rows), so the entered totals are unaffected. 'Část 1' of Tab. 5.1 (pp. 21-23) holds the other faculties; its distinction from 'část 2' was not examined beyond confirming the university total is in část 2a. EQUITY no: the report describes the Centre for Support of Students with Specific Needs (CPSSP), which also serves students from socially or ethnically disadvantaged backgrounds and adapts the form of admission procedures for applicants with specific needs (accommodation such as interpreting or Braille tests), not reserved places, bonus points or lowered thresholds. UPOL faculty admission conditions for 2023/24 were not opened individually - gap.

Equity coded yes on the hardship quota (Haertefallquote / Vorabquote fuer Faelle aussergewoehnlicher Haerte): Staatsvertrag ueber die Hochschulzulassung 2019 Art. 9(1) No. 1 reserves places in every capped procedure for applicants for whom rejection would be an 'aussergewoehnliche Haerte'; Land law implements it for local procedures. It applies only in admission-restricted first-degree programmes (local NC and the central procedure), hence equity_scope some_programmes. Basis: hardship is assessed individually; the recognised grounds are mainly health/disability (illness with a tendency to worsen, career choice restricted by disability) and special social or family circumstances. Limited finances are explicitly NOT a recognised ground (FU Merkblatt), and a severe-disability certificate alone is not sufficient. Basis is therefore coded disability;other (other = individual social/family hardship). CHECKER: this is a judgement call. The quota is a formal reserved-places rule, but eligibility rests on individual hardship rather than membership of a disadvantaged group; the coordinator may prefer to recode it to no, for consistency with countries where individual hardship clauses were not coded. Also present but not coded as an instrument: Nachteilsausgleich (StV Art. 8(2)). On application, the grade or waiting time is replaced by the value the applicant would have reached without hindrances outside their control (illness, disability, pregnancy, family care); this is an individual score correction, not a group threshold. adm_notes: Selectivity (Vipunen open-data API, dataset korkeakoulutus_hakeneet_ja_paikan_vastaanottaneet, updated 2026-09-26; the researcher's script summed programme x selection-queue rows; sums only, no rates): autumn 2023 first-cycle entry, all routes, 95 application targets: places (aloituspaikatLkm) 2822, applications (kaikkiHakijatLkm) 38913, first-preference applicants (ensisijaisetHakijatLkm) 10649, admitted (valitutLkm) 3525, accepted the place (paikanVastaanottaneetLkm) 2738, started studies = entrants (aloittaneetLkm) 2292. Joint application (Yhteishaku) only: places 2680, applications 38511, first-preference 10448, admitted 3434, accepted 2649, started 2205. Spring-2024 starts (Kevät 2024, first cycle; not included in the entered values): places 0, applications 0, admitted 0, started 0. Unit: applications. Each person is counted once per application target, and in the joint application a person may list up to six targets nationally, so the sum over programmes counts persons several times; first-preference applicants are unique persons whose FIRST choice was at this university (a lower bound on unique applicants). Places are published intake capacities per target (some separate-application targets carry no place figure, so the places sum may be incomplete); admitted counts include waiting-list admissions and can exceed places. Regime: national joint application (korkeakoulujen yhteishaku via Opintopolku, Universities Act 36 a §) in which each university sets places and criteria and ranks applicants, while a person receives at most one offer across the joint application by preference order; coded central_allocation (national coordinated system; institution-level counts are published, so rates are computable for this scope and unit). own_admission is an alternative reading, as each university decides its own selection criteria (36 §). Equity: no. National framework (Universities Act 558/2009, Finlex consolidated text read 2026-10-01; 36 § last amended by 1367/2018 and 36 b § by 256/2015, so in force for 2023/24): the university decides its selection criteria; applicants may be split into groups only by educational background; uniform criteria within a group; a limited deviation is allowed only 'Jonkin kieliryhmän koulutustarpeen turvaamiseksi' (to secure a language group's education needs); 36 b § lets universities reserve places for first-time applicants (ensikertalaiset), which is not disadvantage-defined. No national quota, bonus, lowered threshold or separate track for a disadvantage-defined group was found. Institution scan: the full list of autumn-2023 first-cycle application targets and selection-queue types for this university in the Vipunen dataset (queue types in the university extract: Todistusvalinta, Koepisteet, Yhteispisteet, Avoimen väylä, Kilpailumenestys, Jatkuva haku, Muu, Ei valittu, Tieto puuttuu) shows no queue or application target defined by disadvantage; the separate routes found are the open-university route ('Avoimen väylä'; open to anyone completing open-university studies, which charge fees; not disadvantage-defined), competition-success routes, SAT/ACT and international routes, and language-of-instruction targets. SIMHE guidance services for immigrant-background applicants exist (yliopistovalinnat.fi webinar 3.11.2023, for 2024 entry) but are counselling, not an admission rule. Searches (immigrant quota; preparatory-education quota; positive action in admissions) found a 5% quota for graduates of the preparatory programme for immigrants only at universities of applied sciences (e.g. Metropolia, search snippet only), not at these universities. Entrance-exam special arrangements for disability are accommodations, not coded as equity. TAU: the 'Pathway Studies Route' targets are for applicants with foreign school-leaving qualifications who complete the University Pathway Finland online programme (international route, not disadvantage-defined; known from a search snippet of tuni.fi, page not opened). TAU's own 2023 admission documents were not opened - gap.

adm_notes: Source: SIES Parcoursup 2023 open data (session 2023 = entry Sept 2023), summed by script over formations (derived sums, not a published institutional total). applicants = sum of voe_tot (candidates per formation, main + complementary phase; a person applying to several formations of the institution is counted once per formation, so unit = applications); admitted = sum of prop_tot (candidates who received an offer, per formation, same duplication); entrants = sum of acc_tot ('admis' = candidates who accepted the offer; a candidate can hold only one definitive acceptance, so close to persons, but this is acceptance on Parcoursup, not verified enrolment); places = sum of capa_fin. All Parcoursup applicants (néo-bacheliers, reorienting students, other candidates incl. foreign applicants using Parcoursup); not domestic-only. Entry outside Parcoursup (international procedures, direct L2/L3 entry) not included. Includes 'Licence - Droit - Parcours Droit - IED (ex-CAVEJ) - Entièrement en distanciel' (1500 places, 3712 applications, 3561 offers, 1480 accepted, 102 boursiers of 411 néo-bacheliers); without it: places 6141, applications 104023, offers 23465, accepted 6148. Regime 'mixed': national platform; non-selective licences admit within capacity, president ranks only when oversubscribed (L612-3 IV); double licences are selective. Equity: yes = national statutory minimum share of lycée-scholarship holders (bacheliers bénéficiaires d'une bourse nationale de lycée) among candidates retained, Code de l'éducation L612-3 V (non-selective formations when oversubscribed) and VI (selective formations), introduced by the ORE law 2018-166; rates are fixed per formation each year by the academic authority (recteur) and applied by Parcoursup when ordering offers. A ministerial answer published 5 Sept 2023 confirms the 'taux boursiers' apply to more than 12,350 formations. The L612-3 text was read only via a third-party mirror (Légifrance blocked by Cloudflare, not bypassed); the 2023 version was not verified directly. equity_reserved_share_pct left empty: no single institution-wide reserved share is stated; rates vary by formation. equity_filled_entrants = sum of acc_brs (admitted néo-bacheliers holding a lycée scholarship), base = sum of acc_neobac (admitted néo-bacheliers); the dataset's own pct_bours equals acc_brs/acc_neobac. This counts ALL boursiers admitted, not only those admitted because of the minimum rate (no per-institution count of rate-decisive admissions is published; the ministry estimated about 12,300 lycéens nationally for whom the rates were decisive in 2022). Not coded as equity: the statutory maximum share of out-of-académie candidates (residence, not disadvantage), minimum shares of technological/vocational bacheliers in IUT/STS (track, not disadvantage), the 'meilleurs bacheliers' access right (merit), Cordées de la réussite participation (may be considered in file review; holistic), disability accommodations (individual review). Paris 1's own 'Rapport public Parcoursup session 2023' file (28 formation reports, phase principale data at 7 July 2023) states a 'Taux minimum boursier' for each of the 28 formations reported, ranging from 5% to 25% (e.g. Licence Droit 16, Economie 15, Gestion 17, AES 25, Science politique 11, IED law licence 14); not all 41 formations have a report in that file.
